### Model Overview

**MxbAI Embed** is a family of state-of-the-art sentence embedding models by [mixedbread-ai](https://huggingface.co/mixedbread-ai). These models map text into high-quality dense vector representations suitable for semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), clustering, and classification tasks.

All MxbAI Embed models support **Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL)**, which allows flexible dimensionality reduction — you can truncate the output embeddings to smaller sizes (e.g., 512, 256) while retaining strong performance. This enables a cost-performance tradeoff at inference time without retraining.

The family includes English, German, and efficiency-focused variants, ranging from ultra-compact (~24M parameters) to large-scale (~340M parameters).

**Key features:**
- High-quality dense sentence embeddings via BERT-based architectures
- Matryoshka Representation Learning for flexible embedding dimensions
- 2D-Matryoshka variant with both layer and dimension reduction
- Optimized for semantic search, retrieval, clustering, and classification

**References:**
- [mxbai-embed-large-v1](https://huggingface.co/mixedbread-ai/mxbai-embed-large-v1)
- [mxbai-embed-xsmall-v1](https://huggingface.co/mixedbread-ai/mxbai-embed-xsmall-v1)
- [mxbai-embed-2d-large-v1](https://huggingface.co/mixedbread-ai/mxbai-embed-2d-large-v1)

## More Details

* [Mxbai Embedding Quickstart Notebook](coming soon..!)
* [Mxbai Embedding API Documentation](https://keras.io/keras_hub/api/models/bert/)
* [Mxbai Embedding Model Card](https://huggingface.co/mixedbread-ai)
* [KerasHub Beginner Guide](https://keras.io/guides/keras_hub/getting_started/)
* [KerasHub Model Publishing Guide](https://keras.io/guides/keras_hub/upload/)

## Installation

Keras and KerasHub can be installed with:

```
pip install -U -q keras-hub
pip install -U -q keras

```

Jax, TensorFlow, and Torch come preinstalled in Kaggle Notebooks. For instructions on installing them in another environment see the [Keras Getting Started](https://keras.io/getting_started/) page.



---

## Preset Table

| Preset name | Parameters | Description | Base Architecture |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mxbai_embed_large_en` | 335,141,888 | 24-layer MxbAI Embed large English model. Maps sentences to 1024-dimensional dense vectors with Matryoshka representation learning. Trained on high-quality English data. Top-ranked open-source embedding model on the MTEB leaderboard. | BERT-large|
| `mxbai_embed_2d_large_en` | 335,141,888 | 24-layer MxbAI Embed 2D-Matryoshka large English model. Maps sentences to 1024-dimensional dense vectors. Supports both embedding dimension reduction and transformer layer reduction for flexible performance-efficiency tradeoffs. | BERT-large| 
| `mxbai_embed_xsmall_en` | 22,713,216 | 6-layer MxbAI Embed extra-small English model. Maps sentences to 384-dimensional dense vectors with Matryoshka representation learning. Ultra-fast and compact, based on MiniLM-L6-v2 architecture. | MiniLM-L6-v2 |

---

Model Summary
This model is a real-time YOLOv8 Nano object detector specifically fine-tuned for military camouflage soldier detection in challenging outdoors and dense foliage environments. It features a specialized training pipeline incorporating negative background sample injection to minimize ambient false positives. The model is lightweight, optimized for edge inference (e.g., Raspberry Pi 5), and tuned with a custom confidence threshold to prevent false negatives in high-stakes detection scenarios.

Usage
This model is designed for real-time computer vision streams, drone/UAV surveillance feeds, and edge detection systems.

Loading & Inference Code Snippet
Python
from ultralytics import YOLO

# Load the fine-tuned PyTorch model weights
model = YOLO('best_FINAL_v2.pt')

# Run inference on an image or video stream
results = model.predict(
    source='input_image.jpg',
    conf=0.25,        # Optimized threshold to balance precision/recall
    imgsz=640,        # Standard input size
    save=True
)

# Process detected bounding boxes
for result in results:
    boxes = result.boxes.xyxy  # [x1, y1, x2, y2] bounding box coordinates
    scores = result.boxes.conf  # Confidence scores
    classes = result.boxes.cls   # Class IDs
Inputs and Outputs
Input Shape: Tensor of shape (Batch_Size, 3, 640, 640) (RGB images resized to 640×640 pixels).

Output Shape: Tensor of bounding boxes [x1, y1, x2, y2, confidence, class_id] representing localized detections.

Known & Preventable Failures
Extremely Low Resolution: Inputs significantly below 640×640 or severely compressed video feeds may drop detection accuracy for distant personnel.

Heavy Thermal Occlusion: The model relies on RGB visual domain features and will not detect personnel visible solely via infrared/thermal channels without RGB signatures.

System
System Integration: Standalone PyTorch object detection model designed for seamless integration into multi-agent pipelines, ROS2 robotic nodes, or edge REST API servers.

Input Requirements: RGB video stream or image file normalized to standard dynamic ranges (0–255).

Downstream Dependencies: Output bounding box vectors can be passed directly to tracking algorithms (e.g., DeepSORT/ByteTRACK) or secondary agentic alert nodes.

Implementation Requirements
Training Hardware: NVIDIA T4 GPU (Kaggle Cloud Accelerator).

Software Environment: PyTorch, Ultralytics YOLOv8 framework, CUDA 12.x.

Compute Requirements:

Training Duration: 100 Epochs (~45 minutes total compute time).

Inference Speed: Real-time throughput (~30+ FPS on Raspberry Pi 5 edge accelerator; <10ms latency on GPU).

Model Characteristics
Model Initialization
Base Weights: Fine-tuned from pre-trained COCO object detection weights (yolov8n.pt) using transfer learning to accelerate convergence on specialized camouflage features.

Model Stats
Model Architecture: YOLOv8 Nano (yolov8n)

Size: ~6.3 MB (.pt PyTorch format)

Parameters: ~3.2 Million

Layers: 225 backbone/head layers

Latency: ~2.5ms (GPU FP16), ~30ms (Raspberry Pi 5 CPU/Edge)

Other Details
Quantization: Standard FP32 precision; exportable to INT8/FP16 ONNX or NPU formats for edge deployment.

Pruning: Unpruned baseline architecture.

Data Overview
Training Data
The training dataset merges specialized camouflage personnel datasets with negative background samples:

Camouflage Soldier Dataset: Annotated bounding boxes covering various camouflage patterns (woodland, desert, multi-terrain) across diverse environments.

Negative Sample Injection: 37 background images containing zero target objects (empty forests, dense foliage, rocks) were injected without annotations (Null class) to explicitly teach the model to ignore natural noise and reduce false alarms.

Preprocessing & Augmentations: Scaling, translation, horizontal flipping, and Mosaic augmentations.

Demographic Groups
Not applicable. The model is trained exclusively on anonymized imagery focusing on uniform patterns and tactical equipment geometry without identifying individual facial or demographic traits.

Evaluation Data
Split Ratio: 80% Train, 10% Validation, 10% Test.

Distribution: Test set contains balanced samples including extreme occlusion, heavy foliage coverage, and negative background controls to ensure robust evaluation.

Evaluation Results
Summary
The model achieved strong convergence over 100 epochs with high mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5) for camouflage detection. Tuning the confidence threshold to 0.25 drastically minimized false negatives while preserving high precision.

Subgroup Evaluation Results
Dense Foliage / Forest Subgroup: High recall maintained through background negative sample injection.

Open Terrain Subgroup: ~95%+ detection accuracy across standard engagement ranges.

Fairness
Definition: Operational reliability across varying environmental conditions (lighting, foliage density, terrain types).

Metrics: Evaluated on balanced precision-recall curves across distinct environmental backgrounds.

Usage Limitations
Sensitive Use Cases: Intended strictly for research, defense simulation, edge detection prototyping, and surveillance analytics. Must not be relied upon as the sole decision-maker in autonomous lethal hardware systems without human-in-the-loop verification.

Environmental Limitations: Reduced visual performance under complete darkness or severe atmospheric distortion (dense fog, heavy rain) where thermal or radar sensing is required.

Ethics
Risk Identification: Dual-use potential in surveillance applications.

Mitigations: Model safety boundaries and confidence threshold tuning prevent high-confidence false alerts on non-combatants in natural environments. Open-source distribution under permissive licensing ensures research transparency.

Optimized for edge deployment on Raspberry Pi 5 with a 0.25 confidence threshold.

from ultralytics import YOLO

)

# 3. Process and display detection results

    print(f"Detected {len(boxes)} camouflage target(s).")
    for box in boxes:
        print(f"Coordinates: {box.xyxy[0].tolist()} | Confidence: {box.conf[0].item():.2f}")

- Negative
- Neutral

- TF-IDF Vectorization

- Scikit-learn

- Positive

- Neutral

---

## Files

- sentiment_model.pkl

---

Input:

```
The laptop exceeded my expectations. Battery life is amazing.
```

Prediction:

```
Positive
```

- Customer Feedback Analysis
- Sentiment Analysis
- Opinion Mining
- Review Classification
- NLP Projects
- AI Applications

# Review Sentiment Analyzer

This model performs multi-class sentiment classification on English customer reviews using Machine Learning.

## Overview

The model predicts one of three sentiment classes:

- Positive
- Negative
- Neutral

It was trained using TF-IDF feature extraction combined with a Logistic Regression classifier on a synthetic dataset containing 45,647 customer reviews collected across multiple domains.

## Model Details

- **Algorithm:** Logistic Regression
- **Vectorizer:** TF-IDF
- **Framework:** Scikit-learn
- **Language:** English
- **Task:** Text Classification
- **Output Classes:** Positive, Negative, Neutral

## Dataset

Training Dataset: AI Review Sentiment Dataset

- Reviews: 45,647
- Categories: 15
- Countries: 10
- Rating Scale: 1–5 Stars

## Supported Domains

- Electronics
- Mobile Phones
- Laptops
- Restaurants
- Hotels
- Banking
- Software
- Healthcare
- Books
- Movies
- Grocery
- Gaming
- Airlines
- Clothing
- Education

## Input

A customer review written in English.

## Output

- Predicted Sentiment
- Confidence Score

## Example

Input:

"The battery life is amazing and the display is beautiful."

Prediction:

Positive

Confidence:

98.6%

## Limitations

- Supports English reviews only.
- Performance may decrease on sarcastic or highly domain-specific reviews.
- Trained on a synthetic dataset for research and educational purposes.

## Files Included

- sentiment_model.pkl
- tfidf_vectorizer.pkl
- label_encoder.pkl

# Indic S2S frozen-component bundle

A reproducible research bundle for bridge-only Indic speech-to-speech experiments. It contains unmodified frozen checkpoints for:

- Gemma 3 4B IT
- AI4Bharat Indic Parler TTS
- AI4Bharat IndicConformer 600M Multilingual

The bundle also contains MODEL_INDEX.json with source provenance and per-file sizes, plus THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

## Usage

```python
from pathlib import Path
import kagglehub

root = Path(kagglehub.model_download("ivanj0/models/transformers/default/1"))
gemma = root / "gemma-3-4b-it"
conformer = root / "indic-conformer-600m-multilingual"
parler = root / "indic-parler-tts"
```

The companion private research code uses these components stagewise; foundation weights remain frozen and only sequence-aware bridges are trained.

## Licenses and terms

This is a mixed-license bundle, so no single permissive license covers every checkpoint:

- Gemma 3 4B IT: Google Gemma Terms of Use and Prohibited Use Policy apply.
- Indic Parler TTS: Apache License 2.0.
- IndicConformer 600M Multilingual: MIT License.

Downstream users must review and comply with each upstream model's terms. The original model cards and included license files are authoritative. This bundle does not relicense third-party weights.

## Provenance

Exact source handles and upstream repositories are recorded in MODEL_INDEX.json. The files are packaged without model training or weight modification.

# Qwen-AgentWorld

**Qwen-AgentWorld** is a native language world model developed by Qwen (Alibaba Cloud) designed for general agentic environment simulation. Unlike post-hoc environment adapters, Qwen-AgentWorld is trained from Continual Pre-Training (CPT) onward with environment modeling as its primary objective. Given an agent's action and interaction history, Qwen-AgentWorld uses long chain-of-thought reasoning to predict the next environment state across text and GUI interfaces.

## Model Highlights

- **Seven Unified Domains:** Simulates 7 diverse environment domains within a single model: Model Context Protocol (MCP), Search, Terminal/CLI, Software Engineering (SWE), Android, Web, and OS.
- **Native World Model:** Built as an environment simulator from the CPT stage onward, followed by Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL via GSPO).
- **Hybrid MoE Architecture:** Combines Gated DeltaNet linear attention (3:1 ratio with Gated Attention) and sparse Mixture-of-Experts (256 total experts, 8 routed + 1 shared active per layer) for fast, memory-efficient inference.
- **Agent Foundation Capabilities:** Zero-shot generalization to out-of-domain environments (e.g., OpenClaw) and support for multi-turn tool-calling environments.
- **Long Context:** Native support for up to 262,144 tokens (256K context window).

## More Details

* [Qwen AgentWorld Quickstart Notebook](coming soon..!)
* [Qwen AgentWorld API Documentation](https://keras.io/keras_hub/api/models/qwen3_5_moe/)
* [Qwen AgentWorld Model Card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B)
* [KerasHub Beginner Guide](https://keras.io/guides/keras_hub/getting_started/)
* [KerasHub Model Publishing Guide](https://keras.io/guides/keras_hub/upload/)

## Installation

Keras and KerasHub can be installed with:

```
pip install -U -q keras-hub
pip install -U -q keras

```

Jax, TensorFlow, and Torch come preinstalled in Kaggle Notebooks. For instructions on installing them in another environment see the [Keras Getting Started](https://keras.io/getting_started/) page.

---

## Model Presets

| Preset Name | Total Params | Active Params | Description | Architecture | 
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- | 
| `qwen_agentworld_35b_a3b` | **35.1B** | **~3B** | 35B total parameter Qwen-AgentWorld MoE environment simulator model (~3B active parameters per token). Trained across 7 agentic domains. | Qwen3.5 MoE |

# arabic-onnx-chat
![](https://www.googleapis.com/download/storage/v1/b/kaggle-user-content/o/inbox%2F33637499%2Ff7c616e4b07278d802742256d7f5ef4c%2Farabic-onnx-chat.png?generation=1785229140234614&alt=media)
## Overview

**arabic-onnx-chat** هو نموذج محادثة عربي خفيف (Lightweight Arabic Conversational Model) تم تطويره خصيصًا لإنتاج ردود باللغة العربية، مع تركيز على اللهجة الشامية، وتم تصميمه بحيث يكون متوافقًا بشكل كامل مع **ONNX Runtime** للحصول على سرعة عالية أثناء الاستدلال (Inference).

تم تطوير النموذج بواسطة **ONYX AI**، وتم تدريبه على مجموعة بيانات **arabic-shami-chat** التي تم إنشاؤها خصيصًا لهذا المشروع، والتي تحتوي على آلاف أزواج المحادثات بين المستخدم والمساعد باللغة العربية.

---

# Model Architecture

يعتمد النموذج على بنية Transformer Decoder مصغرة تم تطويرها يدويًا باستخدام PyTorch دون الاعتماد على نماذج جاهزة مثل GPT أو LLaMA، مما يجعل النموذج خفيفًا وسريعًا وسهل التحويل إلى ONNX.

يتكون النموذج من الطبقات التالية:

```
Input Tokens
      │
      ▼
AraBERT Tokenizer
      │
      ▼
Token Embedding
      │
      ▼
Positional Embedding
      │
      ▼
Multi-Head Self Attention
(Q, K, V)
      │
      ▼
Residual Connection
      │
      ▼
Layer Normalization
      │
      ▼
Feed Forward Network
(GELU)
      │
      ▼
Residual Connection
      │
      ▼
Layer Normalization
      │
      ▼
Linear Output Layer
      │
      ▼
Vocabulary Logits
```

---

# Layers Description

## 1. AraBERT Tokenizer
![](https://www.googleapis.com/download/storage/v1/b/kaggle-user-content/o/inbox%2F33637499%2F1ee0e2ef48ef076383ccefdaea478e40%2F_28-7-2026_11028_huggingface.co.jpeg?generation=1785229158047326&alt=media)
يعتمد النموذج على **AraBERT v2 Tokenizer** لتحويل النصوص العربية إلى معرفات رقمية (Token IDs)، حيث يقوم بتقسيم الجمل العربية بطريقة مناسبة لطبيعة اللغة العربية مع الحفاظ على الكلمات الشائعة واللواحق.

---

## 2. Token Embedding Layer

تقوم هذه الطبقة بتحويل كل Token إلى متجه رقمي (Embedding Vector) بطول:

- Embedding Dimension = **256**

أي أن كل كلمة يتم تمثيلها داخل فضاء عددي مكون من 256 قيمة.

---

## 3. Positional Embedding

نظرًا لأن طبقات Attention لا تعرف ترتيب الكلمات، تتم إضافة Positional Embeddings لإعطاء النموذج معلومات عن ترتيب الكلمات داخل الجملة.

أقصى طول للجملة:

```
Max Sequence Length = 128
```

---

## 4. Multi-Head Self Attention

تعتبر هذه الطبقة قلب النموذج.

تم استخدام:

- Number of Heads = **4**

ويتم إنشاء ثلاث مصفوفات أساسية:

- Query (Q)
- Key (K)
- Value (V)

ثم يتم حساب درجات الانتباه باستخدام المعادلة:

\[
Attention(Q,K,V)=Softmax\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V
\]

كما يستخدم النموذج **Causal Mask** لمنع النموذج من رؤية الكلمات المستقبلية أثناء التدريب، مما يجعله مناسبًا لمهام توليد النصوص.

---

## 5. Residual Connection

بعد طبقة Attention يتم إضافة الناتج إلى الإدخال الأصلي (Residual Connection)، مما يساعد على تحسين استقرار التدريب وتقليل مشكلة تلاشي التدرج (Vanishing Gradient).

---

## 6. Layer Normalization

يتم استخدام Layer Normalization بعد كل من طبقة Attention وطبقة Feed Forward لتسريع عملية التدريب وتحسين استقرار النموذج.

---

## 7. Feed Forward Network (FFN)

تتكون الشبكة الأمامية من طبقتين Fully Connected:

```
256
   │
Linear
   │
512
   │
GELU
   │
Linear
   │
256
```

ويتم استخدام دالة التنشيط:

```
GELU
```

بدلاً من ReLU لأنها تحقق أداءً أفضل في نماذج Transformer.

---

## 8. Output Projection

في النهاية يتم استخدام طبقة:

```
Linear(256 → Vocabulary Size)
```

لتحويل المخرجات إلى احتمالات لجميع الكلمات الموجودة في القاموس (Vocabulary).

---

# Training Dataset

تم تدريب النموذج باستخدام مجموعة البيانات:

**arabic-shami-chat**

وهي مجموعة بيانات تم تطويرها بواسطة فريق المشروع، وتحتوي على محادثات باللغة العربية مع تركيز على اللهجة الشامية.

تعتمد البيانات على أزواج من:

- Prompt
- Response

حيث يتعلم النموذج إنتاج الرد المناسب اعتمادًا على الرسالة السابقة.

صيغة البيانات:
![](https://www.googleapis.com/download/storage/v1/b/kaggle-user-content/o/inbox%2F33637499%2F0bbb045a476ca199f5c142aa8cb73704%2F_28-7-2026_11343_www.kaggle.com.jpeg?generation=1785229223795083&alt=media)
---

# Training Strategy

تم تدريب النموذج بطريقة **Autoregressive Language Modeling**.

```
# UI APP
![](https://www.googleapis.com/download/storage/v1/b/kaggle-user-content/o/inbox%2F33637499%2F997edfb7882240c961b8ed731241d46b%2F1.png?generation=1785229335115009&alt=media)
